summary: This edition provides 84 complete documentation guides and 2 additional screened leads. 40 earlier screened entries received full guides. New and updated records carry their own dated evidence checks. Spatial-audio generation, film captions and camera-driven production illustrate different kinds of control. SAID maps detected sound events onto a panoramic view. Kdenlive’s subtitle workflow gives an editor text and timing inside an established non-linear editor. Other guides cover image-to-geometry handoffs, fabrication, lyric and notation drafts, and accessible media. Velo adds locally generated rehearsal textures to its live graph. ZigZag adds canvas-pinned feedback and version comparison for an AI-directed embroidery edit. Software licensing is reviewed independently of model terms, any paid service or required proprietary host. Documentation and published examples informed the quality checks. No discovered app was installed or run. The frozen plan covered 114 fields with 1306/1306 repository queries attempted. 1306 completed successfully, 0 were partial, and 0 failed. 253 were bounded. All 33 configured model tasks were attempted. 0 model tasks failed. The collection retained explicit warnings and limits. Metadata screening indexed all 2,779 saved repository pages, spanning 83,958 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog was consulted alongside today's metadata, including earlier pilot candidates. It currently has 117,114 raw records and 1,132 previously screened pending guides. A metadata signal does not establish software eligibility. Unreviewed and excluded candidates remain in private research records. Live primary research captured 460 usable responses from 600 distinct URL attempts, including non-GitHub primary sources in 114 of 114 fields. 8 captures were size-bounded. The ecosystem notes record each configured source group. The notes identify limits such as access and rate restrictions, failed fetches and bounded discovery pages. The counts represent the documented searches and available pages. Evidence label counts were 0 Recommended, 1 Ready to try, 80 Quality unverified, 5 Experimental. SAID meets the Ready to try criteria for the stated scope. The public Hugging Face Space at the checked revision, with the bundled examples and the released SAID PaSST checkpoint for noncommercial research. Credential-pattern material in unsealed source captures was redacted before sealing. The original and redacted content hashes and provenance stay in the local evidence record. 31 model tasks reached the configured maximum of 50 returned rows each. The model listings are bounded discovery leads. Model-task responses with no rows: text2text-generation, zero-shot-audio-classification. The separate watchlist and evidence enrichment recorded 63 individual watchlist failures and 4 evidence failures. Source failures are retained as gaps.

Audacity documents a local neural editing workflow with separate transcription and enhancement effects. KU Leuven provides an institution-specific setup route. The Intel plugin’s published installer and a newer distribution have different compatibility evidence. 7 primary-source requests failed or returned unusable content.

SolidCraft documents editable parametric sketches and an optional agent connection. Shape Studio separately documents local image-to-GLB or OBJ inference. Mesh export alone gives no evidence of watertightness or production print tolerances.
The browser LLM study and WebGPU documentation describe compute options. Hardware adapters, browser versions and cached weights affect any particular local creative workflow.

Imprimatur's primary site demonstrates an image-to-roller geometry pathway. The reviewed page alone did not establish a neural step, file-level licenses or a physical material test.
Current primary work separates the sequence of strokes from an image of the completed painting. A generated stroke program has a different verification burden from a flattened image.

HueForge's Unity documentation separates grouped recoloring and masks from optional AI palette and texture generation via a configured provider. Host and service requirements differ across these routes.

The stereo style-transfer paper treats the left and right views together. Test corresponding edges and viewing comfort before considering a result suitable for exhibition.

Semantic Gaussians links foundation-model features to editable 3D selections. One Feature 3DGS path was unavailable. Export and reliable masking need verification in the individual package. 1 primary-source request failed or returned unusable content.

World-Shaper describes handling the spatial structure of panoramas. Inspect seams and geometry on the intended projection or headset before relying on a generated world.
Learning-based cloth work and ContourCraft tackle drape and interpenetration. Fit on a rig and physical pattern cutting remain separate checks.

A current research paper tests detectors under specific synthesis families and perturbations. Model confidence on new footage and creative utility are separate claims from benchmark performance.

Imprimatur's relief roller preview is useful context. It provides no proof of ordinary press imposition, bleed, color management or an open learned process from this pass. 1 primary-source request failed or returned unusable content.
AlayaWorld presents playable generated video world research. This source establishes an experimental method and does not by itself verify a maintained game authoring package or reusable assets.
Current neural audio research separates waveform synthesis from usable patch authoring. Patches need checked sample rates, inputs and predictable routing in the target environment.

The neural photon-mapping and indirect-light research pages show different treatments of glossy effects and caustics. Their comparisons do not establish support in a specific renderer or real-time device.

Current tactile generation studies and AltCanvas illustrate prompt-guided image creation. Tactile standards still require clarity, distinguishable features and a physical or user review. SVG export alone does not meet that bar. 1 primary-source request failed or returned unusable content.

ComicTL describes a custom YOLO-Nano bubble detector and a separate translation step. Match text, lettering and reading order to the source page after the detections.

Ossia and QLC+ document timeline/control options. The camera model's detections and the behavior of a real console or fixture are distinct verification tasks.

WaivePulse describes an offline suite. A captured product page does not establish every underlying model grant or seamless playback at chosen tempos.
The inverse procedural yarn study reconstructs parameters from images down to fiber detail. A visual yarn model does not give verified physical fiber composition or production tolerances.
StegaStamp describes hiding information in imagery intended for digital display or printing. Paper, capture and lighting conditions matter when evaluating whether the decoded mark survives.

The Diorama authors document single-view scene reconstruction. Hidden surfaces and unobserved dimensions remain uncertain even when the composition looks plausible.

eManuSkript describes browser tools for manuscript research. Booklet documentation is useful for imposition, while learned scan-to-EPUB tools have a separate OCR role and require page-by-page proofing. The Rosette design app inspected here describes electronics GDSII, outside book design.

SpriteLoom documents a diffusion path into Aseprite. GridFab and Pixelbolt describe separate agent-editable structures. Files or drawing actions can be deterministic even when a connected agent selects those actions.

Duke's work concerns learned robotic shadow silhouettes. CUNY and Sunway document separate puppet preservation and performance research. None of those contexts by itself clears transferable production code.

OmniScore-Bench evaluates symbol recognition, musical structure and interpretation separately. Audiveris and LilyPond documentation provide distinct transcription and engraving context. 3 primary-source requests failed or returned unusable content.

Project documentation distinguishes learned landmark estimation, geometric warping and photometric correction. The Cyber-Sync source maps browser camera landmarks to display graphics. Field conditions such as reflection, capture latency and projector geometry need separate testing. 1 primary-source request failed or returned unusable content.

The DiffPC paper frames projector color correction as diffusion conditioned on the target and surroundings. Its public code and configuration were available. A separate paper’s software release carries an academic or non-profit noncommercial restriction. These findings leave on-site color matching and deployment reproducibility open. 4 primary-source requests failed or returned unusable content.

AMBIT documents 44.1 kHz FOA generation and editing. PhysWave documents explicit trajectories and short 16 kHz FOA clips. SAID estimates event direction on a panoramic map. Each has a separate model or data review, and the physical or headphone decoder needs its own listening comparison. 2 primary-source requests failed or returned unusable content.
